newsitem.title: FRANCE: Union calls Air France Europe strike for Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: Union calls Air France Europe strike for Oct 16.

text.p: France's communist-led CGT union said on Friday it was calling for a 24-hour strike at Air France Europe on October 16 to protest about jobs and pay.
The union said it was urging all staff at the state airline's domestic and regional subsidiary to halt work from 2000 GMT on October 16 to 1959 GMT on October 17.
The CGT union represents around 30 percent of ground staff including mechanics, reservation and administrative employees, a CGT spokesman said.
An Air France Europe spokeswoman declined comment on the strike call. She said the CGT ranked second to the SNPIT in the last elections for the works committee.

An SNPIT union spokesman said his union had already called out members for October 17 as part of a national stoppage called by civil servants and public sector workers to protest against the government's austerity budget for 1997.

The chairman of the Air France group, Christian Blanc, is merging Air France Europe into the main international airline, axing its loss-making domestic routes and cutting pilots' salaries to bring them into line with those of Air France, around 15 percent less.
Some 950 jobs among ground staff will be cut as part of the merger plan.
